records.source: Οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·
records.gloss: No therefore now condemnation to the [ones] in Christ Jesus;
pieces: So then, those who are in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus now face no sentence of condemnation.

L.1: So now [there is] no condemnation for those in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.

R.1: So now God does not condemn those who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. No sentence of punishment hangs over them.

decisions.choice: condemnation: the sentence passed on the guilty, and the penalty it carries
decisions.reason: katakrima is a law-court word: the judge's verdict against someone and the punishment that follows. Paul used it in 5:16 and 5:18, where Adam's trespass led to condemnation for all. Here that verdict is gone for those in Christ.

decisions.choice: "so now": a conclusion, and a new time
alternatives: "now" as only "at this point in the argument"
decisions.reason: ara draws the conclusion of what Paul has said since 5:12, and especially of 7:25. "Now" is the time that began with Christ, as in 3:21 ("but now") and 5:9: what was true of life under sin is no longer true.

decisions.choice: in Christ Jesus: joined to him, sharing his death and life
decisions.reason: Paul has said that believers were baptized into Christ, died with him and live with him (6:3-11). Being "in" him is that union, and the verdict that falls on him now falls on them.

decisions.choice: the verse ends at "in Christ Jesus"
alternatives: adds "who walk not according to the flesh" (and, in later copies, "but according to the Spirit")
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts end the verse here. Later copies add words from verse 4, so that the verse no longer says that freedom from condemnation depends on being in Christ alone; the longer form is in the King James Version. The SBLGNT has the short text. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: face no sentence of condemnation (B); God does not condemn them, no sentence of punishment (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the word is a judge's sentence (m1). Readable names God as the judge, since he alone passes this sentence (verse 33).

decisions.choice: who belong to Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in Christ Jesus" as belonging to him (m3).

records.heading: Set free by the Spirit of life

records.source: ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν σε ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου.
records.gloss: The for law of the Spirit of the life in Christ Jesus set free you from the law of the sin and of the death.
pieces: For in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus the law of the Spirit who gives life has freed you from the law of sin and death.

L.2: For the law of the Spirit of life in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus set you free from the law of sin and of death.

R.2: The Spirit gives life to everyone who is joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. And the Spirit's power has set you free from the power of sin, which leads to death.

decisions.choice: law: here a ruling power or order, the Spirit's against sin's
alternatives: the law of Moses in both places: the same law, used by the Spirit or by sin
decisions.reason: Paul has just spoken of "another law" at work in his body, "the law of sin" (7:21-23). Here he sets the rule of the Spirit against that rule of sin. Some read both phrases as the law of Moses, which sin used to bring death (7:10-11) and which the Spirit now fulfills (verse 4); the wording allows that too.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of life: the Spirit who gives life
alternatives: "the spirit of life" as a quality, a living spirit
decisions.reason: Paul names the Spirit as the one who gives life in verses 10-11, against sin which leads to death.

decisions.choice: "in Christ Jesus" goes with the whole saying: the Spirit sets free those joined to Christ
alternatives: goes only with "life": the life that is in Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: The phrase stands between "life" and "set free" and may go with either. Both say that the freedom and the life come in union with Christ (verse 1), so the levels keep it close to both.

decisions.choice: "you" (singular)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have "you" in the singular, Paul speaking to each reader in turn; some have "me", continuing chapter 7, and a few "us". The SBLGNT has "you". (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: the Spirit's power; the power of sin
alternatives: the Spirit's law; the law of sin
decisions.reason: Readable says "power" for the sense the meaning decision prefers (m1), so a new reader does not think of a written law code; the decision is marked uncertain for reviewers.

records.source: τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου, ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός, ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί, ἵνα τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου πληρωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα·
records.gloss: The for impossible [thing] of the law, in which it was weak through the flesh, the God the of himself Son having sent in likeness of flesh of sin and concerning sin condemned the sin in the flesh, \v 4 so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, the [ones] not according to flesh walking but according to Spirit;
pieces: The law was powerless, since the flesh had left it weak. So God acted. He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, as an offering for sin, and in the flesh {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} passed sentence on sin.
He did this so that the law's righteous requirement would be fully met in us, who conduct our lives by the Spirit and not by the flesh.

L.3: For what was impossible for the law, in that it was weak through the flesh, God [did]: sending {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son in [the] likeness of flesh of sin, and for sin, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} condemned sin in the flesh,
L.4: so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to [the] flesh but according to [the] Spirit.

R.3: The law could not do this, because our sinful selves were too weak to keep it. But God did it. He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son as a real human being, with a body like the bodies of sinful people. God sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be an offering for sin. In {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} human body God judged sin and condemned it.
R.4: God did this so that what the law rightly requires would come true in us. Now we do not follow our sinful selves. We follow the Spirit.

decisions.choice: what the law could not do, God did
alternatives: "the law's weakness" as the object of "condemned"
decisions.reason: The sentence opens with "the impossible thing of the law" and never gives it a verb of its own; Paul breaks off and says what God did instead. The thing the law could not do is what verse 2 has just said: set people free from sin and death.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature, weak and under sin's sway
decisions.reason: In Romans 7-8 the flesh is human life in its weakness, under sin's sway and set against God's Spirit (7:5, 7:18, 7:25; Galatians 5:16-17). Paul does not mean the body as such, which God will give life to (verse 11). The law was good (7:12), but it could not change people whose flesh was ruled by sin.

decisions.choice: in the likeness of sinful flesh: truly human, yet not himself sinful
decisions.reason: homoiōma ("likeness") lets Paul say two things at once. The Son came in real human flesh, the flesh in which sin rules in everyone else; yet he did not sin (2 Corinthians 5:21). Paul uses the same word in Philippians 2:7.

decisions.choice: for sin: as a sin offering
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament "for sin" is the regular name for the sin offering (Leviticus 4-5, 16; Isaiah 53:10). God sent the Son to be the sacrifice that deals with sin.

decisions.choice: condemned sin in the flesh: in the Son's own human nature, where sin was judged
decisions.reason: God passed sentence on sin in the very flesh where it had ruled. Because "the flesh" follows the Son coming "in the likeness of sinful flesh", it most naturally means his flesh, put to death on the cross; sin's condemnation fell there, and so not on those in Christ (verse 1).

decisions.choice: the righteous requirement is fulfilled in us: God brings it about
alternatives: "fulfilled by us" through our own effort
decisions.reason: dikaiōma is what the law rightly requires. The verb is passive and the phrase is "in us", not "by us": God's work in Christ and the Spirit bring about what the law asked for. Those in whom this happens are those who live by the Spirit.

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: peripateō ("walk") is the usual biblical word for how a person lives, as in 6:4 and 13:13.

decisions.choice: the sentence is broken into four
decisions.reason: The Greek runs on from verse 3 into verse 4 and leaves its first phrase without a verb (m1). Balanced finishes that thought first, "The law was powerless", and then tells what God did in short sentences.

decisions.choice: our sinful selves
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m2), as in Galatians 5 and Romans 13:14.

decisions.choice: as a real human being, with a body like the bodies of sinful people; in his human body
decisions.reason: Readable explains "likeness of sinful flesh" (m3) and "in the flesh" (m5) in plain words.

decisions.choice: conduct our lives
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the picture of walking means (m7).

records.source: οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ὄντες τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς φρονοῦσιν, οἱ δὲ κατὰ πνεῦμα τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος.
records.gloss: The [ones] for according to flesh being the [things] of the flesh set mind on, the [ones] but according to Spirit the [things] of the Spirit.
pieces: Those who are under the rule of the flesh have their minds fixed on the concerns of the flesh, but those under the rule of the Spirit, on the concerns of the Spirit.

L.5: For those who are according to [the] flesh set [their] minds on the things of the flesh, but those [who are] according to [the] Spirit, on the things of the Spirit.

R.5: People who live by their sinful selves think only about what their sinful selves want. But people who live by the Spirit think about what the Spirit wants.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature under sin's sway, set against the Spirit
decisions.reason: In Romans 7-8 the flesh is human life in its weakness, under sin's sway and set against God's Spirit (7:5, 7:18, 7:25; Galatians 5:16-17). Paul does not mean the body as such, which God will give life to (verse 11).

decisions.choice: set the mind on: the whole bent of thought, will and desire
alternatives: think about, as a passing thought
decisions.reason: phroneō is not only thinking but what a person is set on and lives for, as in Philippians 3:19 ("their minds set on earthly things").

decisions.choice: being according to the flesh: having one's existence shaped and ruled by it
decisions.reason: Paul describes two kinds of people, those whose life is ruled by the flesh and those ruled by the Spirit. The second half of the verse leaves out the verbs, which carry over from the first.

decisions.choice: under the rule of
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "being according to" means (m3).

decisions.choice: their sinful selves
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m1).

records.source: τὸ γὰρ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος, τὸ δὲ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος ζωὴ καὶ εἰρήνη·
records.gloss: The for mindset of the flesh death, the but mindset of the Spirit life and peace;
pieces: The outlook of the flesh means death, but the outlook of the Spirit means life and peace.

L.6: For the mindset of the flesh [is] death, but the mindset of the Spirit [is] life and peace.

R.6: When the sinful self is in charge of what you think about, the end is death. When the Spirit is in charge, there is life and peace.

decisions.choice: mindset: the way of thinking and wanting that belongs to the flesh or to the Spirit
alternatives: the mind as a part of a person
decisions.reason: phronēma is the noun from the verb of verse 5: a settled way of thinking and desiring.

decisions.choice: death, life and peace: separation from God, and life with him
alternatives: physical death and long life only
decisions.reason: Death here is more than the end of the body: it is the wages of sin (6:23), being cut off from God now and at the end. Life is the life of the age to come, already begun (verse 10), and peace is peace with God (5:1) and the wholeness that follows from it.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature under sin's sway
decisions.reason: In Romans 7-8 the flesh is human life in its weakness, under sin's sway and set against God's Spirit (7:5, 7:18, 7:25; Galatians 5:16-17). Paul does not mean the body as such, which God will give life to (verse 11).

decisions.choice: outlook
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "outlook" for a settled way of thinking and wanting (m1).

decisions.choice: when the sinful self is in charge of what you think about
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means (m3) and turns "the mindset of" into a plain clause.

records.source: διότι τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς ἔχθρα εἰς θεόν, τῷ γὰρ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑποτάσσεται, οὐδὲ γὰρ δύναται·
records.gloss: Because the mindset of the flesh hostility toward God, to the for law of the God not it submits, not even for it is able;
pieces: That is because the outlook of the flesh is at war with God. It does not bow to God's law, and in fact it is not able to.

L.7: Because the mindset of the flesh [is] hostility toward God, for it does not submit to the law of God, nor indeed is it able [to].

R.7: The sinful self is God's enemy. It refuses to obey God's law, and it could never obey it.

decisions.choice: hostility: enmity, being an enemy
decisions.reason: echthra is the state of enemies at war. Paul has said that we were God's enemies before he reconciled us (5:10).

decisions.choice: the subject of "does not submit" and "is not able" is the mindset of the flesh
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular and continue from "the mindset of the flesh". Paul is not saying that people cannot ever turn to God; he says that the flesh, as such, will never submit to God's law.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature under sin's sway
decisions.reason: In Romans 7-8 the flesh is human life in its weakness, under sin's sway and set against God's Spirit (7:5, 7:18, 7:25; Galatians 5:16-17). Paul does not mean the body as such, which God will give life to (verse 11).

decisions.choice: is at war with God (B); is God's enemy (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the strength of the word for enmity (m1).

decisions.choice: the sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means (m3).

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται.
records.gloss: The [ones] and in flesh being God to please not are able.
pieces: People who are in the flesh have no power to please God.

L.8: And those who are in [the] flesh are not able to please God.

R.8: People who are ruled by their sinful selves cannot do what pleases God.

decisions.choice: in the flesh: in the old state ruled by sin
decisions.reason: Paul said "when we were in the flesh" of the life before Christ (7:5). He still lives in a body (Galatians 2:20), so "in the flesh" here is the state of life ruled by sin, not having a body.

decisions.choice: please God: be acceptable to him, do what he approves
decisions.reason: areskō is to please someone, to win their approval, as in 1 Thessalonians 4:1.

decisions.choice: ruled by their sinful selves
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in the flesh" means (m1).

records.source: Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ἀλλὰ ἐν πνεύματι, εἴπερ πνεῦμα θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: You but not are in flesh but in Spirit, if indeed Spirit of God dwells in you.
pieces: But you are not in the flesh; you are in the Spirit, if God's Spirit really does live in you.

L.9: But you are not in [the] flesh but in [the] Spirit, if indeed [the] Spirit of God dwells in you.

R.9: But you are not ruled by your sinful selves. The Spirit rules you, if God's Spirit really lives in you.

decisions.choice: if indeed: a condition Paul assumes is met, with a gentle check
decisions.reason: eiper ("if indeed") assumes the readers do have the Spirit, while reminding them that this is what being in the Spirit depends on. Paul uses it again in verse 17.

decisions.choice: in the flesh, in the Spirit: two ways of existing, each with its ruling power
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, "in the flesh" is the old life ruled by sin; "in the Spirit" is the new life where God's Spirit lives and rules.

decisions.choice: dwells: lives in, makes a home in
decisions.reason: oikeō is to live in a house. Paul pictures the Spirit at home in the believer, as God dwelt among his people (1 Corinthians 3:16).

decisions.choice: ruled by your sinful selves; the Spirit rules you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two phrases mean (m2).

records.source: εἰ δέ τις πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἔχει, οὗτος οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: If but anyone Spirit of Christ not has, this [one] not is of him.
pieces: If anyone lacks the Spirit of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, that person is not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}.

L.9: But if anyone does not have [the] Spirit of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, this [one] is not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}.

R.9: Anyone who does not have the Spirit of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is not one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God is the Spirit of Christ
alternatives: a different spirit, such as Christ's attitude
decisions.reason: In one breath Paul calls the same Spirit "the Spirit of God" and "the Spirit of Christ" (verses 9-11), as in Galatians 4:6 ("the Spirit of his Son"). The Spirit belongs to the Father and to the Son.

decisions.choice: his: Christ's
decisions.reason: The pronoun points back to Christ, just named: whoever lacks his Spirit does not belong to him.

records.source: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, τὸ μὲν σῶμα νεκρὸν διὰ ἁμαρτίαν, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωὴ διὰ δικαιοσύνην.
records.gloss: If but Christ in you, the indeed body dead because of sin, the but Spirit life because of righteousness.
pieces: But if {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is in you, the body is marked for death because of sin, but the Spirit is life for you because of righteousness.

L.10: But if {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [is] in you, the body [is] dead because of sin, but the Spirit [is] life because of righteousness.

R.10: But if {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} lives in you, your body will still die because of sin. But the Spirit gives you life, because of the righteousness God has given you.

decisions.choice: the Spirit, God's Spirit, is life
decisions.reason: pneuma could be the believer's own spirit, alive while the body dies. But Paul writes "life", a noun, not "alive", and in verses 2, 6 and 11 it is God's Spirit who gives life. So the sense is most likely that the Spirit is life for the believer.

decisions.choice: the body is dead: mortal, bound to die because of sin
decisions.reason: Verse 11 calls the same bodies "mortal". Since Adam, death came to all because of sin (5:12), and believers' bodies still die; but God will give them life.

decisions.choice: because of righteousness: God's gift of right standing with him
alternatives: the righteous life the Spirit produces
decisions.reason: In Romans righteousness is above all what God gives in Christ, the right standing of 5:17 and 5:21 ("grace reigning through righteousness to eternal life"). It may include the righteous life that follows (6:18), but the contrast with "because of sin" points to God's verdict.

decisions.choice: Christ in you: the same as the Spirit dwelling in you
decisions.reason: Paul moves from "the Spirit of God dwells in you" to "Christ in you" without a break. Christ lives in believers by his Spirit.

decisions.choice: marked for death
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "dead" means here (m2): the body is bound to die, not already a corpse.

decisions.choice: the righteousness God has given you
decisions.reason: Readable says whose righteousness it is (m3).

records.source: εἰ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐγείραντος τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ νεκρῶν οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν, ὁ ἐγείρας ἐκ νεκρῶν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ζῳοποιήσει καὶ τὰ θνητὰ σώματα ὑμῶν διὰ τὸ ἐνοικοῦν αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα ἐν ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: If and the Spirit of the [one] having raised Jesus out of dead dwells in you, the [one] having raised out of dead Christ Jesus will give life also to the mortal bodies of you because of the dwelling of him Spirit in you.
pieces: And if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead has made a home in you, then God, who raised {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus from the dead, will bring your mortal bodies to life as well, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit lives in you.

L.11: And if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from [the] dead dwells in you, the one who raised {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus from [the] dead will give life also to your mortal bodies because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit who dwells in you.

R.11: God raised Jesus from death. If God's Spirit lives in you, then God, who raised {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus from death, will also give life to your bodies, which now must die. He will do this because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit lives in you.

decisions.choice: will give life to your mortal bodies: the resurrection of the body
decisions.reason: The verb is future and the object is the mortal body, the body that dies (verse 10). Paul means that God will raise believers as he raised Jesus (6:5, 1 Corinthians 15:22).

decisions.choice: because of his Spirit who dwells in you
alternatives: "through his Spirit who dwells in you"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts are divided between two forms that differ by one ending: "because of his Spirit" (the SBLGNT) and "through his Spirit". The first gives the Spirit's presence as the reason God will raise the body; the second makes the Spirit the one through whom he does it. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: the one who raised Jesus: God
decisions.reason: Paul describes God by what he did in raising Jesus, as in 4:24. The verse names the Father, the Son and the Spirit together.

decisions.choice: if: a condition Paul assumes is true of his readers
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, Paul speaks of what is true for his readers, while saying what it depends on.

decisions.choice: God, who raised
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, whom the phrase describes (m3).

decisions.choice: God raised Jesus from death; your bodies, which now must die
decisions.reason: Readable states first the fact the condition rests on, then the promise, and explains "mortal".

records.source: Ἄρα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ὀφειλέται ἐσμέν, οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆν, εἰ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆτε μέλλετε ἀποθνῄσκειν, εἰ δὲ πνεύματι τὰς πράξεις τοῦ σώματος θανατοῦτε, ζήσεσθε.
records.gloss: So then, brothers, debtors we are, not to the flesh, of the according to flesh to live, \v 13 if for according to flesh you live, you are about to die; if but by Spirit the deeds of the body you put to death, you will live.
pieces: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we are under an obligation, but not to the flesh, to live as the flesh dictates.
If you live as the flesh dictates, you are headed for death. But if by the Spirit you keep putting the body's practices to death, you will live.

L.12: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to [the] flesh.
L.13: For if you live according to [the] flesh, you are going to die; but if by [the] Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

R.12: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we do owe something, but we owe nothing to our sinful selves. We do not have to live the way they want.
R.13: If you live the way your sinful self wants, you will die. But if, with the Spirit's power, you keep killing off the sinful things you do with your body, you will live.

decisions.choice: we are debtors, not to the flesh: the debt is owed to God's Spirit, though Paul does not finish the thought
decisions.reason: Paul says only to whom we owe nothing. The rest of the sentence, and verses 2-11, show that what believers owe is to live by the Spirit who gives them life.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature under sin's sway, set against the Spirit
decisions.reason: As in verses 3-9, the flesh is human life ruled by sin and opposed to the Spirit, not the body as such.

decisions.choice: you are going to die: death as the end of that way of life, cut off from God
alternatives: only bodily death, which comes to all
decisions.reason: Everyone dies in the body, including those who live by the Spirit (verse 10). The contrast with "you will live", the life of verses 6 and 11, shows that Paul means death in the full sense, the wages of sin (6:23).

decisions.choice: the deeds of the body: sinful practices carried out through the body
decisions.reason: Paul has spoken of sin reigning in the mortal body and using its members (6:12-13). The "deeds of the body" are what the body does under that rule; the body itself is not evil.

decisions.choice: by the Spirit you put to death: the Spirit is the power, and the killing goes on
decisions.reason: The dative "by the Spirit" gives the means: believers do this in the Spirit's strength, not their own. The present tense of the verb points to something done again and again, not once for all.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow believers, women and men
decisions.reason: Paul addresses the whole church in Rome as members of one family, as in 1:13 and 7:1; the plural includes the sisters.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The inclusive default names everyone Paul addresses (m6); the traditional setting keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: keep putting to death (B); keep killing off (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the ongoing action of the present tense (m5).

decisions.choice: the sinful things you do with your body; your sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the deeds of the body" (m4) and "flesh" (m2) mean here.

records.heading: God's children by the Spirit

records.source: ὅσοι γὰρ πνεύματι θεοῦ ἄγονται, οὗτοι υἱοί εἰσιν θεοῦ.
records.gloss: As many as for by Spirit of God are led, these sons are of God.
pieces: Those whom God's Spirit is leading are God's {{gender:children|sons}}.

L.14: For as many as are led by [the] Spirit of God, these are {{gender:children|sons}} of God.

R.14: All the people God's Spirit leads are God's own {{gender:children|sons}}.

decisions.choice: sons: the standing of a son and heir, given to women and men alike
decisions.reason: huios is the word for a son, and in a family it carried the standing of a son and heir. Paul gives that standing to every believer, women and men alike (Galatians 3:26-29), and in verses 16-17 he says the same with the word for children, which has no gender.

decisions.choice: led: guided day by day
decisions.reason: agō is to lead or guide. The present tense describes the Spirit's ongoing direction of a believer's life, the life of putting sin to death in verse 13 (compare Galatians 5:18).

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The word gives the standing of a son and heir (m1), which Paul gives to men and women alike. The inclusive default says who has it; the traditional setting keeps "sons", which shows the standing more plainly.

records.source: οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ·
records.gloss: Not for you received a spirit of slavery again to fear, but you received Spirit of adoption as sons, in whom we cry: Abba, the Father;
pieces: What you received was not a spirit of slavery that would put you back under fear. You received the Spirit of adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}, and in the Spirit we call out, "Abba, Father!"

L.15: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery [bringing you] back into fear, but you received [the] Spirit of adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}, by whom we cry, "Abba, Father!"

R.15: When God gave you the Spirit, God did not make you slaves again, living in fear. By giving you the Spirit, God gave you adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}. And by the Spirit we cry out to God, "Abba! Father!"

decisions.choice: a spirit of slavery: the Spirit they received is not one who enslaves
decisions.reason: Paul is not saying that they received a spirit of slavery before. He sets the Spirit they did receive against what that Spirit is not: one who would make them slaves again, as they were under sin (6:17-20). The lowercase shows that the phrase names what the Spirit is not.

decisions.choice: adoption as sons: being made a son and heir by law
alternatives: the feeling of being God's children
decisions.reason: huiothesia is the legal word for adoption. In Roman law an adopted son received the full rights of a son born into the family, including the inheritance (verse 17). Paul gives that standing to every believer, women as much as men (Galatians 4:5-7).

decisions.choice: Abba: the Aramaic word for "father", followed by the Greek word
decisions.reason: Abba is the Aramaic word a child used for a father, and the word Jesus used in his own prayer (Mark 14:36). The churches kept the Aramaic word and added its translation, as Galatians 4:6 also does. Believers address God the way the Son does.

decisions.choice: by whom we cry: in the Spirit's power we call God Father
alternatives: a new sentence beginning "By him we cry", leading into verse 16
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuation joins "in whom we cry" to the Spirit of adoption. krazō is to cry out aloud, here in prayer. In Galatians 4:6 it is the Spirit who cries; here "we" do, by the Spirit.

decisions.choice: from "you" to "we"
decisions.reason: Paul says "you received" and then "we cry": he and his readers pray in the same way, Jew and Gentile alike.

decisions.choice: adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The word gives the standing of a son and heir (m2), which Paul gives to men and women alike. The inclusive default says who is adopted; the traditional setting keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: God gave you the Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable names the giver, God, so the sentence can say plainly what he did and did not do.

decisions.choice: slave(s), slavery
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: a spirit of slavery set against the Spirit of adoption as children.

records.source: αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα συμμαρτυρεῖ τῷ πνεύματι ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐσμὲν τέκνα θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Itself the Spirit bears witness with the spirit of us that we are children of God.
pieces: The Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} joins our own spirit in testifying that we are God's children.

L.16: The Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of God.

R.16: The Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} agrees with what our own spirit says: we are God's children.

decisions.choice: our spirit: the believer's own human spirit
decisions.reason: Paul sets "the Spirit himself" beside "our spirit", so the second is the human spirit, the inner self that prays "Abba" (verse 15).

decisions.choice: bears witness with: two witnesses agree
decisions.reason: summartureō is to testify together with someone. The Spirit adds his witness to that of our spirit, so that two witnesses confirm the matter, as the law required (Deuteronomy 19:15). Some read it as the Spirit testifying to our spirit; the word itself means "with".

decisions.choice: children: the word for children, of either sex
decisions.reason: teknon has no gender. Paul moves from "sons" (verse 14) to "children" without changing the sense: those who belong to God's family.

decisions.choice: the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: The Greek pronoun is neuter only because the word for spirit is neuter. The Spirit is a person who testifies, prays and searches, so he is never called "it".

records.source: εἰ δὲ τέκνα, καὶ κληρονόμοι· κληρονόμοι μὲν θεοῦ, συγκληρονόμοι δὲ Χριστοῦ, εἴπερ συμπάσχομεν ἵνα καὶ συνδοξασθῶμεν.
records.gloss: If and children, also heirs: heirs indeed of God, joint-heirs and of Christ, if indeed we suffer with [him] so that also we may be glorified with [him].
pieces: If we are children, we are also heirs. We are God's heirs, and we inherit alongside {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, if we suffer together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that we will also be glorified together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.17: And if children, also heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, if indeed we suffer with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] so that we may also be glorified with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].

R.17: And because we are God's children, we will receive everything God has promised to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children. We will receive it together with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. But we must suffer with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} now, so that we will also share {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory later.

decisions.choice: heirs: those who will receive the inheritance
decisions.reason: Children inherit from their father. The inheritance God promised Abraham was the world (4:13); for believers it is the coming glory of verse 18 and the renewed creation of verse 21.

decisions.choice: if indeed we suffer with him: suffering with Christ is part of belonging to him
alternatives: a doubt whether they will suffer
decisions.reason: eiper (as in verse 9) states a condition Paul expects to be met. Those who share Christ's inheritance share his path, through suffering to glory.

decisions.choice: so that we may also be glorified with him: suffering leads to glory
decisions.reason: hina gives the purpose and goal: suffering with Christ is the road to sharing his glory, as verse 18 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: we will receive everything God has promised; share his glory later
decisions.reason: Readable explains what being an heir means (m1) and what being glorified with Christ means.

records.source: Λογίζομαι γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς.
records.gloss: I reckon for that not worthy the sufferings of the now time toward the about-to-be glory to be revealed to us.
pieces: I have weighed it up: what we suffer in this present time does not begin to balance the glory that is going to be revealed to us.

L.18: For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time [are] not worthy [to be set] against the coming glory to be revealed to us.

R.18: We suffer now. But I am sure that our suffering is very small next to the glory God will show us in the future.

decisions.choice: not worthy: not of equal weight
decisions.reason: axios first meant "of equal weight" on a pair of scales. Set beside the coming glory, present sufferings weigh almost nothing (2 Corinthians 4:17).

decisions.choice: I reckon: I have thought it through and conclude
decisions.reason: logizomai is a word for careful reckoning, the same word as "counted" in chapter 4. Paul states a settled judgment.

decisions.choice: revealed to us: shown to us and given to us
decisions.reason: eis can mean "to", "toward" or "upon". The glory will be shown to believers and they will share it (verse 17); the passive leaves God as the one who reveals it.

decisions.choice: the present time: the time between Christ's coming and his return
decisions.reason: Paul calls this "the now time" (3:26, 11:5): already the age of salvation, yet still a time of suffering and waiting (verses 22-25).

decisions.choice: does not begin to balance
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of weighing on scales (m1).

decisions.choice: God will show us
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who reveals the glory (m3).

records.heading: Creation waits to be set free

records.source: ἡ γὰρ ἀποκαραδοκία τῆς κτίσεως τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκδέχεται·
records.gloss: The for eager expectation of the creation the revelation of the sons of the God awaits;
pieces: The created world cranes its neck in longing, waiting for God's {{gender:children|sons}} to be revealed.

L.19: For the eager longing of the creation awaits the revelation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of God.

R.19: Everything God made is waiting eagerly for the day when God shows who {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:children|sons}} really are.

decisions.choice: the creation: the world God made, apart from human beings
decisions.reason: ktisis is what God created. Here it groans and waits but did not choose its state (verse 20), and believers are named separately (verse 23), so Paul means the non-human creation, which shares humanity's fall and its hope (Genesis 3:17-18).

decisions.choice: eager longing: watching with head stretched forward
decisions.reason: apokaradokia pictures someone craning the neck to see what is coming. Paul speaks of creation as a person waiting for something it cannot yet see.

decisions.choice: revelation: the moment when God's children are shown for what they are
decisions.reason: Believers are already God's children (verse 16), but this is hidden. At the end it will be made plain, when they share Christ's glory (Colossians 3:4).

decisions.choice: sons: the standing of a son and heir, given to women and men alike
decisions.reason: huios is the word for a son, and in a family it carried the standing of a son and heir. Paul gives that standing to every believer, women and men alike (Galatians 3:26-29), and in verses 16-17 he says the same with the word for children, which has no gender.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 14: the inclusive default names everyone who has this standing (m4), and the traditional setting keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: cranes its neck in longing
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in the word (m2).

records.source: τῇ γὰρ ματαιότητι ἡ κτίσις ὑπετάγη, οὐχ ἑκοῦσα ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὑποτάξαντα, ἐφ’ ἑλπίδι ὅτι καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ κτίσις ἐλευθερωθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς δουλείας τῆς φθορᾶς εἰς τὴν ἐλευθερίαν τῆς δόξης τῶν τέκνων τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: To the for futility the creation was subjected, not willingly but because of the [one] having subjected, in hope \v 21 that also itself the creation will be set free from the slavery of the decay into the freedom of the glory of the children of the God.
pieces: Creation was made subject to futility. This was not its own choice; it was because of the one who subjected it. Yet there was hope:
creation itself will also be released from its slavery to decay and will enter the freedom that comes with the glory of God's children.

L.20: For the creation was subjected to futility, not of its own will but because of the one who subjected [it], in hope
L.21: that the creation itself also will be set free from the slavery of decay into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

R.20: Creation was made subject to things that come to nothing. It did not choose this. God made it so, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also gave creation hope.
R.21: One day creation will be set free from decay, which holds it like a slave. Then creation will share the freedom of God's children, when they receive their glory.

decisions.choice: futility: emptiness, failing to reach its purpose
decisions.reason: mataiotēs is what is empty and comes to nothing, the word of Ecclesiastes 1:2 in the Greek Old Testament ("vanity of vanities"). Creation cannot be what it was made to be.

decisions.choice: the one who subjected it: God, when he cursed the ground
decisions.reason: Paul refers to Genesis 3:17-19, where God cursed the ground because of Adam. Only God could subject creation "in hope". Some think of Adam, whose sin brought this about; but the hope fits God, who judged and promised at once.

decisions.choice: that creation will be set free: the content of the hope
decisions.reason: hoti can mean "that" or "because". Read as "that", it says what creation hopes for; read as "because", it gives the reason for hope. The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: the slavery of decay: bondage to decay and death
decisions.reason: phthora is decay and corruption, everything that falls apart and dies. Creation is held by it as a slave is held.

decisions.choice: the freedom of the glory of the children of God: the freedom that comes when they are glorified
alternatives: the glorious freedom of God's children
decisions.reason: The phrase links freedom with the glory of verse 18. Creation will share the freedom that God's children enter when their glory is revealed.

decisions.choice: God made it so, but he also gave creation hope
alternatives: because of the one who subjected it
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who subjected creation (m2) and so needs a deity pronoun for him.

decisions.choice: things that come to nothing
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word (m1).

decisions.choice: slave(s), slavery
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: slavery to decay set against the freedom of the glory of God's children (8:21).

records.source: οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις συστενάζει καὶ συνωδίνει ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν·
records.gloss: We know for that all the creation groans together and travails together until the now;
pieces: We know that all creation, to this very day, groans as one and suffers the pains of giving birth together.

L.22: For we know that all the creation groans together and suffers birth pains together until now.

R.22: We know that everything God made has been crying out in pain until now, like a woman giving birth to a baby.

decisions.choice: groans and suffers birth pains: pain that leads to new life
decisions.reason: Birth pains are a common biblical picture for the distress before God's new age (Isaiah 26:17-19; Mark 13:8). They hurt, but they mean something is about to be born.

decisions.choice: together: all the parts of creation together
decisions.reason: The verbs begin with "with" (syn-). The most natural sense is that the whole creation groans as one; Paul adds "we too" only in verse 23.

decisions.choice: like a woman giving birth to a baby
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of birth pains (m1).

records.source: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἔχοντες ἡμεῖς καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς στενάζομεν, υἱοθεσίαν ἀπεκδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν τοῦ σώματος ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Not only and, but even ourselves the firstfruit of the Spirit having, we also ourselves in ourselves groan, adoption as sons awaiting, the redemption of the body of us.
pieces: And not creation alone. We ourselves, who have the Spirit as the first share of the harvest, also groan within ourselves while we long for our adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}, when our body will be redeemed.

L.23: And not only [that], but even we ourselves, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, we also groan within ourselves, eagerly awaiting adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}, the redemption of our body.

R.23: And we groan too. God has given us the Spirit as the first part of all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give us. But we still groan inside, because we are waiting for our full adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}: the day when God will set our bodies free.

decisions.choice: firstfruits: the first part of the harvest, a pledge of the rest
decisions.reason: Israel brought the first sheaf of the harvest to God (Leviticus 23:10). It was part of the crop and promised that the rest was coming. The Spirit is God's first gift of the life to come, and the promise of the rest.

decisions.choice: the firstfruits of the Spirit: the firstfruits that are the Spirit
alternatives: the first share of the Spirit, with more of the Spirit to come
decisions.reason: Paul does not mean a first portion of the Spirit; the Spirit himself is the first part of the harvest, as in 2 Corinthians 1:22 the Spirit is the down payment.

decisions.choice: adoption still awaited: the full and public act of adoption
alternatives: a different adoption from that of verse 15
decisions.reason: Believers have already received adoption (verse 15), but they wait for it to be completed, when the body is raised. Paul often speaks of salvation as given now and still to come.

decisions.choice: the redemption of our body: the body set free from death
decisions.reason: apolutrōsis is release, especially of a slave or captive at a price (3:24). Here it is the body's release from decay and death at the resurrection, not escape from the body.

decisions.choice: "adoption" stands in the text
alternatives: leaves out "adoption": "eagerly awaiting the redemption of our body"
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts leave out the word for adoption, perhaps because verse 15 says believers already have it. Most manuscripts have it, and the SBLGNT keeps it. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 15: the inclusive default names everyone adopted, and the traditional setting keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: the first share of the harvest (B); the first part of all that he will give us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the picture of the firstfruits (m1).

decisions.choice: our full adoption
decisions.reason: Readable adds "full" because believers have already been adopted (m3).

records.source: τῇ γὰρ ἐλπίδι ἐσώθημεν· ἐλπὶς δὲ βλεπομένη οὐκ ἔστιν ἐλπίς, ὃ γὰρ βλέπει τίς ἐλπίζει;
records.gloss: In the for hope we were saved; hope but being seen not is hope, what for sees anyone does he hope?
pieces: It was in hope that we were saved. But a hope that is already in sight is no hope at all. Who goes on hoping for what is already in front of them?

L.24: For in hope we were saved. But hope being seen is not hope; for what anyone sees, who hopes [for it]?

R.24: God saved us, and so we have hope for what is still to come. If we can already see something, we do not need to hope for it. No one hopes for something that is already there.

decisions.choice: in hope we were saved: salvation came with a future still to be seen
alternatives: saved by hope, as if hope were the means
decisions.reason: Paul says that people are saved through faith (Ephesians 2:8), so the dative here is not the means. Salvation came to believers with hope attached: much of it is still to come.

decisions.choice: "who hopes for what he sees?"
alternatives: "why does anyone still hope for what he sees?"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ slightly in the question at the end of the verse. The sense is the same: no one hopes for what is already seen. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no one"
decisions.reason: Paul asks a question with an obvious answer. The levels keep the question at Literal and Balanced; Readable gives the answer.

decisions.choice: God saved us
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who saves.

decisions.choice: No one hopes for something that is already there
alternatives: who hopes for what he sees?
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer Paul's question expects (m3).

records.source: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ βλέπομεν ἐλπίζομεν, δι’ ὑπομονῆς ἀπεκδεχόμεθα.
records.gloss: If but what not we see we hope for, through endurance we eagerly await.
pieces: But if what we hope for is something we do not yet see, we keep waiting for it with endurance.

L.25: But if we hope for what we do not see, we eagerly await [it] with endurance.

R.25: But we hope for things we cannot see yet. So we keep on waiting for them, and we do not give up.

decisions.choice: endurance: holding out under pressure
decisions.reason: hupomonē is the steady endurance of someone under strain, the word of 5:3-4. Waiting for what is not yet seen takes it.

decisions.choice: eagerly await: wait with longing for what is sure to come
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verses 19 and 23: creation and believers wait for the same thing.

decisions.choice: we do not give up
decisions.reason: Readable says what endurance means in plain words (m1).

records.source: Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα συναντιλαμβάνεται τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ ἡμῶν· τὸ γὰρ τί προσευξώμεθα καθὸ δεῖ οὐκ οἴδαμεν, ἀλλὰ αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα ὑπερεντυγχάνει στεναγμοῖς ἀλαλήτοις, ὁ δὲ ἐραυνῶν τὰς καρδίας οἶδεν τί τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος, ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων.
records.gloss: Likewise and also the Spirit helps with the weakness of us; the for what we should pray as is necessary not we know, but itself the Spirit intercedes on behalf with groanings unspoken; \v 27 the [one] and searching the hearts knows what [is] the mindset of the Spirit, that according to God he intercedes on behalf of holy [ones].
pieces: In the same way, the Spirit also lends a hand in our weakness. What we should pray for, and how, we do not know. But the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} pleads on our behalf, with groans that no words carry.
And God, who looks deep into hearts, knows what the Spirit intends, because the Spirit pleads for God's holy people in line with what God wants.

L.26: And likewise the Spirit also takes hold with [us] in our weakness; for what we should pray, as is fitting, we do not know, but the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} intercedes on [our] behalf with unspoken groanings.
L.27: And the one who searches the hearts knows what the mindset of the Spirit [is], because [the Spirit] intercedes for [the] holy ones according to God.

R.26: In the same way, the Spirit helps us when we are weak. We do not know what we should pray for, or how to pray. But the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} prays to God for us. The Spirit groans in ways that words cannot say.
R.27: God sees what is in our hearts, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows what the Spirit is thinking. The Spirit prays for God's people in the way God wants.

decisions.choice: likewise: as hope sustains us, so the Spirit helps us
decisions.reason: Paul has said that hope keeps believers waiting (verses 24-25). In the same way the Spirit helps them while they wait and groan (verse 23).

decisions.choice: helps: takes hold of a load together with someone
decisions.reason: sunantilambanomai pictures someone taking the other end of a heavy load, as Martha wanted Mary to help her (Luke 10:40). The Spirit does not take the weakness away; he shares the weight.

decisions.choice: what we should pray, as we ought: both what to ask and how
decisions.reason: The phrase "as is fitting" follows the question of what to pray. Believers do not know what to ask in a way that fits God's will, or how to ask it.

decisions.choice: unspoken groanings: groans that are never put into words
alternatives: groanings too deep to be put into words
decisions.reason: alalētos can mean "not spoken" or "that cannot be spoken". Either way the Spirit's pleading goes beyond words. The word does not describe speaking in tongues, which uses words of a kind.

decisions.choice: intercedes, without "for us"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "for us" after the verb; the earliest leave it out, and the SBLGNT follows them. The verb itself already means pleading on someone's behalf, so the sense is the same. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: the one who searches the hearts: God
decisions.reason: The Old Testament speaks of God as the one who sees and tests the heart (1 Samuel 16:7; Psalm 139:1; Jeremiah 17:10). Paul uses that description here.

decisions.choice: because: God knows the Spirit's mind because the Spirit prays as God wills
alternatives: "that": God knows that the Spirit prays as he wills
decisions.reason: hoti can give the reason or the content of what God knows. The sense is close either way: the Spirit's prayer and God's will agree.

decisions.choice: according to God: in keeping with God's will
decisions.reason: The short phrase means "as God wants", as in 2 Corinthians 7:9-11 ("grief according to God").

decisions.choice: holy ones: God's people, set apart for him
decisions.reason: hagioi are all believers, called to be holy (1:7), not a few outstanding ones.

decisions.choice: the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; "the Spirit" repeated
decisions.reason: The Greek pronouns are neuter only because the word for spirit is neuter. English repeats "the Spirit" where it would need a pronoun, and says "the Spirit himself", never "it".

decisions.choice: God, who looks deep into hearts (B); God sees what is in our hearts (R)
alternatives: the one who searches the hearts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, whom the phrase describes (m6).

records.heading: The Spirit pleads for us

records.source: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσι τὸν θεὸν πάντα συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν, τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν.
records.gloss: We know and that to the [ones] loving the God all things work together for good, to the [ones] according to purpose called being.
pieces: We know that, for people who love God, all things work together and lead to good. They are the ones called in keeping with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} purpose.

L.28: And we know that to those who love God all things work together for good, to those who are called according to [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] purpose.

R.28: We know that in the lives of those who love God, all things work together to bring about good. These are the people God has called, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned.

decisions.choice: no word "God" as the subject of "works together"
alternatives: "God works all things together for good"
decisions.reason: Some early and important manuscripts add "God" after the verb, so that God is the subject: "God works all things together for good". Most manuscripts do not have it, and the SBLGNT leaves it out. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: "all things" is the subject: all things work together for good
alternatives: God is the unnamed subject: "he works in all things for good"
the Spirit of verses 26-27 is the subject
decisions.reason: In the text without "God", "all things" most naturally serves as the subject. Some take God, or the Spirit just mentioned, as the subject and "all things" as what he works in. On every reading, the good comes about because of God and his purpose, named in the same verse; things do not work for good by themselves.

decisions.choice: good: the good God intends, which verse 29 names
alternatives: comfort or success in this life
decisions.reason: The good is not that everything turns out pleasantly. Verses 29-30 say what it is: being made like God's Son and sharing his glory, even through the sufferings of verses 17-18 and 35-36.

decisions.choice: according to purpose: God's purpose
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "according to purpose", but the calling is God's (verse 30), so the purpose is his, as in 9:11.

decisions.choice: the called: those who love God are those God called
decisions.reason: The second phrase describes the same people as the first, from God's side: they love God because he called them.

decisions.choice: [his] purpose (L); his purpose, as he planned (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs to say whose purpose it is (m4); Literal brackets the word the Greek lacks.

records.heading: Called according to God's purpose

records.source: ὅτι οὓς προέγνω, καὶ προώρισεν συμμόρφους τῆς εἰκόνος τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πρωτότοκον ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς·
records.gloss: Because whom he foreknew, also he predestined conformed of the image of the Son of him, for the to be him firstborn among many brothers;
pieces: Those God knew beforehand {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also marked out beforehand to be shaped into the image of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, so that the Son would be the firstborn among many {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

L.29: Because those whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} foreknew, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also predestined [to be] conformed to the image of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be firstborn among many {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

R.29: Long before, God already knew those who would be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}. He decided then that they would be made just like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. So the Son would be the first and most honored among many {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

decisions.choice: foreknew: knew and chose beforehand, in a relationship
alternatives: knew in advance what people would do
decisions.reason: In the Bible God's "knowing" people often means choosing them and setting his love on them (Amos 3:2). Paul uses the same verb of Israel in 11:2, "his people whom he foreknew".

decisions.choice: predestined: decided beforehand, marked out in advance
decisions.reason: proorizō is to set a boundary or decide something ahead of time. Here God decides beforehand what those he knew will become: like his Son.

decisions.choice: conformed to the image of his Son: sharing the Son's form and glory
decisions.reason: The phrase includes the change of character that begins now (2 Corinthians 3:18) and the glorified body to come (Philippians 3:21, the same word). Humans were made in God's image (Genesis 1:27); the Son is that image (2 Corinthians 4:4).

decisions.choice: firstborn: first in time and first in rank
decisions.reason: The firstborn had the place of honor and the double share (Psalm 89:28 in Hebrew numbering, of the king). Christ is also the first to rise from the dead (Colossians 1:18), and others will follow him.

decisions.choice: brothers: the members of God's family, women and men
decisions.reason: Those conformed to the Son become his brothers and sisters, God's family.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The inclusive default names the whole family (m5); the traditional setting keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: knew beforehand, marked out beforehand (B); decided then (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say in plain words what the two verbs mean (m1, m2). Literal keeps the traditional words.

decisions.choice: the first and most honored
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "firstborn" means here (m4).

records.source: οὓς δὲ προώρισεν, τούτους καὶ ἐκάλεσεν· καὶ οὓς ἐκάλεσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδικαίωσεν· οὓς δὲ ἐδικαίωσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδόξασεν.
records.gloss: Whom and he predestined, these also he called; and whom he called, these also he justified; whom and he justified, these also he glorified.
pieces: And those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} marked out beforehand, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also called. Those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also declared righteous. And those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} declared righteous, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also glorified.

L.30: And those whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} predestined, these {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also called; and those whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called, these {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also justified; and those whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} justified, these {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also glorified.

R.30: Those God decided on ahead of time, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also called. Those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also put right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. And those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also gave a share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

decisions.choice: called: God's call that brings people to himself
alternatives: an invitation that may be refused
decisions.reason: In Paul "called" means God's effective call through the gospel, which brings people to faith (1:6-7, 9:24; 1 Corinthians 1:24).

decisions.choice: justified: declared righteous by God
decisions.reason: dikaioō is the verb of 3:24-26 and 5:1: God declares the ungodly righteous through faith in Christ (4:5).

decisions.choice: glorified: a future glory spoken of as already done
decisions.reason: Glory is still to be revealed (verses 17-18, 21). Paul uses the past tense because, in God's purpose, it is as certain as the calling and justifying that have already happened.

decisions.choice: declared righteous
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "justify" means (m2), as elsewhere in Romans.

decisions.choice: put right with himself; gave a share in his glory
decisions.reason: Readable says "put right with himself" for justify, as in 3:24-26, and explains "glorified" as being given a share in God's glory (m3).

records.source: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν πρὸς ταῦτα;
records.gloss: What then will we say to these [things]?
pieces: So what is our response to all this?

L.31: What then will we say to these things?

R.31: So what can we say about all this?

decisions.choice: these things: everything Paul has said, especially in chapter 8
decisions.reason: Paul often asks "What then will we say?" to draw a conclusion (4:1, 6:1). Here he answers with the questions of verses 31-35.

records.heading: If God is on our side

records.source: εἰ ὁ θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, τίς καθ’ ἡμῶν;
records.gloss: If the God for us, who against us?
pieces: If God is on our side, who can stand against us?

L.31: If God [is] for us, who [is] against us?

R.31: If God is on our side, no one can win against us.

decisions.choice: if: since God is for us
alternatives: a real doubt whether God is for us
decisions.reason: Paul states a condition he holds to be true, as verse 32 shows.

decisions.choice: who is against us: no one who can prevail
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one". Believers do have enemies (verses 35-36), but none who can stand against God.

decisions.choice: no one can win against us
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects (m2).

records.source: ὅς γε τοῦ ἰδίου υἱοῦ οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πάντων παρέδωκεν αὐτόν, πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν χαρίσεται;
records.gloss: Who indeed the own Son not spared, but for us all handed over him, how not also with him the all things to us will he freely give?
pieces: God did not hold back even {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son, but handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over for us all. How could {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fail, then, to give us everything along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a free gift?

L.32: He who indeed did not spare {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son but handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over for us all, how will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not also with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} freely give us all things?

R.32: God did not keep back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son. He gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up to die for all of us. So we can be sure that God will also give us everything else, along with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.

decisions.choice: did not spare his own Son: as Abraham did not withhold Isaac
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament the angel says to Abraham, "you did not spare your beloved son" (Genesis 22:12, 16), with the same verb. What Abraham was spared, God did.

decisions.choice: handed over: gave up to death
decisions.reason: paradidōmi is the verb of 4:25, "handed over because of our trespasses", and of the passion accounts. God gave his Son over to die.

decisions.choice: freely give: give as an act of grace
decisions.reason: charizomai is to give freely, from the same root as grace. If God gave the greatest gift, he will give the rest.

decisions.choice: a question expecting "he certainly will"
decisions.reason: Paul argues from the greater to the lesser: the question means that God will certainly give believers everything with his Son.

decisions.choice: gave him up to die
decisions.reason: Readable says what "handed over" means (m2).

decisions.choice: So we can be sure that God will also give us everything
alternatives: how will he not also give us all things?
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects (m4).

records.source: τίς ἐγκαλέσει κατὰ ἐκλεκτῶν θεοῦ;
records.gloss: Who will bring a charge against chosen [ones] of God?
pieces: Who will bring any accusation against those God has chosen?

L.33: Who will bring a charge against [the] chosen ones of God?

R.33: Who can accuse the people God has chosen?

decisions.choice: bring a charge: accuse in court
decisions.reason: enkaleō is a law-court word: to bring a formal charge. Paul pictures the final judgment.

decisions.choice: chosen ones: those God has chosen for himself
decisions.reason: eklektoi is the Old Testament name for God's people (Isaiah 65:9). It sums up verses 29-30.

decisions.choice: a question, answered by the next sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 33-35 are a series of questions. The SBLGNT reads the words after each question as Paul's answer.

records.source: θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν·
records.gloss: God the [one] justifying;
pieces: God is the one who declares them righteous.

R.33: It is God who puts them right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

decisions.choice: a statement: God is the one who justifies
alternatives: a question: "Will God, who justifies, bring a charge?"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates these words as an answer. Some read them as a further question expecting "no". Either way, the judge who declares believers righteous will not accuse them (Isaiah 50:8-9, which this passage echoes).

decisions.choice: God who justifies: an echo of Isaiah 50:8
decisions.reason: The servant of the LORD says, "He who vindicates me is near; who will contend with me?" Paul uses the same law-court picture.

decisions.choice: declares them righteous
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "justify" means, as in verse 30; it supplies "them", the chosen ones.

decisions.choice: puts them right with himself
decisions.reason: Readable uses the wording of verse 30.

records.source: τίς ὁ κατακρινῶν;
records.gloss: Who [is] the [one] condemning?
pieces: Who is going to condemn them?

L.34: Who [is] the one who will condemn?

R.34: Who will say they are guilty and must be punished?

decisions.choice: the one who will condemn: future
decisions.reason: The same letters can be read as a present or a future participle; the SBLGNT accents it as future, looking to the last judgment.

decisions.choice: say they are guilty and must be punished
decisions.reason: Readable says what "condemn" means, as in verse 1.

records.source: Χριστὸς ὁ ἀποθανών, μᾶλλον δὲ ἐγερθείς, ὅς καί ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν·
records.gloss: Christ the [one] having died, rather and having been raised, who also is at right hand of the God, who also intercedes for us;
pieces: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is the one who died; still more, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was raised, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is at the right hand of God, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pleads on our behalf.

L.34: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [is] the one who died, and more than that, was raised, who also is at [the] right hand of God, who also intercedes for us.

R.34: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} died, and more than that, God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to life. Now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has the place of honor at God's right side, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks to God for us.

decisions.choice: an answer: Christ, who died and pleads for us, is the one who could condemn and does not
alternatives: a further question: "Is it Christ who died ... who will condemn us?"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates the words as a statement. Read either way, the point is the same: the one who might judge is the one who died for us and speaks for us.

decisions.choice: "Christ"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have "Christ Jesus"; others have "Christ" alone, which the SBLGNT follows. Some also add "from the dead" after "raised". (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: at the right hand of God: the place of honor and power
decisions.reason: The words echo Psalm 110:1, "Sit at my right hand". To sit at a king's right hand was to share his rule.

decisions.choice: intercedes: pleads on someone's behalf
decisions.reason: entugchanō is to approach someone for another, the verb used of the Spirit in verse 27. The Spirit pleads within believers, and Christ pleads for them before God (Hebrews 7:25).

decisions.choice: God raised him to life; the place of honor at God's right side
alternatives: was raised; at the right hand of God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raised him and explains "right hand" (m3).

records.source: τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ;
records.gloss: Who us will separate from the love of the Christ?
pieces: Who can tear us away from the love of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}?

L.35: Who will separate us from the love of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?

R.35: Can anything take us away from the love {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has for us?

decisions.choice: the love of Christ: Christ's love for us
decisions.reason: The question is whether anything can cut believers off from the love Christ has for them, as verse 37 ("the one who loved us") and verse 39 ("the love of God") show.

decisions.choice: "of Christ"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts have "the love of God", as in verse 39. Most have "of Christ", and the SBLGNT follows them. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: who: any person or thing
decisions.reason: The question begins with "who", but the list that follows names things, not people. Paul means anything at all.

decisions.choice: Can anything
decisions.reason: Readable says "anything", since the list that follows names things (m3).

records.source: θλῖψις ἢ στενοχωρία ἢ διωγμὸς ἢ λιμὸς ἢ γυμνότης ἢ κίνδυνος ἢ μάχαιρα;
records.gloss: Trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?
pieces: Trouble, or anguish, or persecution? Hunger, or lack of clothing, or danger, or the sword?

L.35: Trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?

R.35: Can troubles or hard times? Can people who attack us because we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}? Can hunger, or having nothing to wear, or danger, or a violent death?

decisions.choice: trouble and distress: outward pressure and inner anguish
decisions.reason: thlipsis is pressure and hardship; stenochōria is being hemmed in, with nowhere to turn. Paul pairs them in 2:9.

decisions.choice: sword: violent death, as by execution
decisions.reason: The sword stands for being killed by force, the fate of martyrs, as verse 36 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: persecution, famine, nakedness: what Paul himself had suffered
decisions.reason: Paul lists such hardships from his own life in 2 Corinthians 11:23-27. These are things that might seem to show that God had abandoned his people.

decisions.choice: people who attack us because we belong to Christ; a violent death
decisions.reason: Readable explains "persecution" and "sword" (m2) in plain words.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ, whose love verse 35 speaks of, and the title takes the usual setting.

records.source: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Ἕνεκεν σοῦ θανατούμεθα ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα σφαγῆς.
records.gloss: As it has been written that: For the sake of you we are being put to death whole the day, we were counted as sheep of slaughter.
pieces: As it is written, "On {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} account we are being killed the whole day through; we are looked on as sheep for the butcher."

L.36: Just as it is written, "For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sake we are being put to death all the day; we were counted as sheep of slaughter."

R.36: This is what the Scriptures say: "Because we belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, people try to kill us all the time. They think of us as sheep to be killed."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 44:23 (Hebrew numbering)
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the psalm in the words of the Greek Old Testament. There God's people, faithful to him, cry out that they suffer for his sake. Paul applies their words to believers who suffer for Christ.

decisions.choice: "you" is God, to whom the psalm is spoken
decisions.reason: The psalm addresses God. Paul keeps its words; in his use, suffering "for your sake" is suffering for belonging to God and to Christ.

decisions.choice: all the day: all the time, continually
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying "without stopping".

decisions.choice: sheep of slaughter: sheep meant to be killed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew phrase means sheep set aside for slaughter, with no defense.

decisions.choice: Because we belong to you, people try to kill us
alternatives: for your sake we are put to death
decisions.reason: Readable says why they suffer and who causes it.

records.source: ἀλλ’ ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς.
records.gloss: But in these [things] all we more than conquer through the [one] having loved us.
pieces: But in all of this we are winning, and winning by far, through the one who loved us.

L.37: But in all these things we are winning overwhelmingly through the one who loved us.

R.37: But even in all these troubles, we win a complete victory with the help of the one who loved us.

decisions.choice: win overwhelmingly: win and more than win
decisions.reason: hupernikaō adds "beyond" to the verb "conquer". Believers do not only survive these things; through Christ's love they win a victory greater than the enemy's attack.

decisions.choice: the one who loved us: Christ, whose love is named in verse 35
alternatives: God, whose love is named in verse 39
decisions.reason: The past tense points to a single act of love, Christ's death (Galatians 2:20). Paul speaks of the same love as Christ's and God's (verses 35, 39), so the levels keep "the one who loved us".

decisions.choice: in all these things: in the middle of them, not by escaping them
decisions.reason: The victory is won while the troubles of verse 35 go on.

decisions.choice: winning overwhelmingly (L); winning, and winning by far (B); a complete victory (R)
decisions.reason: The familiar wording "more than conquerors" goes back to older English Bibles. The levels say in current words what the verb means (m1).

records.source: πέπεισμαι γὰρ ὅτι οὔτε θάνατος οὔτε ζωὴ οὔτε ἄγγελοι οὔτε ἀρχαὶ οὔτε ἐνεστῶτα οὔτε μέλλοντα οὔτε δυνάμεις οὔτε ὕψωμα οὔτε βάθος οὔτε τις κτίσις ἑτέρα δυνήσεται ἡμᾶς χωρίσαι ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: I am persuaded for that neither death nor life nor angels nor rulers nor things present nor things coming nor powers \v 39 nor height nor depth nor any creation other will be able us to separate from the love of the God the [one] in Christ Jesus the Lord of us.
pieces: For I am fully persuaded that not death and not life, not angels and not rulers, not what is here now and not what is yet to come, not any powers,
not what is high above and not what is deep below, nor any other created thing, will be able to cut us off from God's love, which is ours in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.

L.38: For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers,
L.39: nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from the love of God that [is] in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.

R.38: I am sure of this: not death, not life, not angels, not spirit rulers, not what is happening now, not what will happen later, not any powers,
R.39: not anything above us or below us, not anything else God has made, nothing at all can ever take us away from God's love. We have that love because we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.

decisions.choice: I am persuaded: I have become convinced and remain so
decisions.reason: The perfect tense of peithō describes a settled conviction.

decisions.choice: angels, rulers, powers: spiritual beings
decisions.reason: Paul uses "rulers" and "powers" for spiritual forces in Ephesians 6:12 and Colossians 2:15, and here they stand beside angels. Whatever their rank, none of them can come between believers and God's love.

decisions.choice: height and depth: all space, above and below
alternatives: terms from astrology for the stars' high and low points
decisions.reason: The words can name the heights of heaven and the depths beneath the earth (compare Psalm 139:8). In astrology the same words were used of the stars' positions, which some believed ruled human life; Paul may include that idea. Either way, nowhere in all creation is beyond God's love.

decisions.choice: any other created thing: anything else in creation
decisions.reason: ktisis here is anything created. Everything that might threaten believers is itself something God made.

decisions.choice: "powers" after "things to come"
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts move "powers" next to "rulers", where it seems to belong; the earliest have it after "things to come", and the SBLGNT follows them. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: the love of God that is in Christ Jesus: God's love, given and known in union with Christ
decisions.reason: God's love is the love shown in Christ's death (5:8) and enjoyed by those joined to him. The chapter ends where it began, with those who are "in Christ Jesus" (verse 1).

decisions.choice: what is high above, what is deep below
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the two words mean (m3).

decisions.choice: spirit rulers
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of rulers are meant (m2).

decisions.choice: We have that love because we belong to Christ Jesus our Lord
decisions.reason: Readable ends with a short sentence that says what "in Christ Jesus" means (m6).
